title: Turing's 1950 prediction, read closely
summary: In 1950 Turing predicted that in about fifty years computers could play the imitation game well enough that an average interrogator would have no more than a 70 percent chance of a right identification after five minutes.

beats.say: In nineteen fifty, Turing predicted a test with a five minute limit.
The paper was Computing Machinery and Intelligence, from nineteen fifty.
It described an imitation game with a machine and an interrogator.
He predicted that in about fifty years, computers could play it well.
With a storage capacity of about ten to the ninth.
An average interrogator would have no more than a seventy percent chance of a right call.

data.label: chance of a right identification (at most)

beats.say: That means at least three calls in ten would be wrong.
Turing set a time limit and a threshold, both stated in numbers.
Claims of passing can be checked against those two numbers: five minutes, seventy percent.
The prediction is short and specific. That makes it testable.

facts.claim: In his 1950 paper Turing predicted that in about fifty years computers with a storage capacity of about 10^9 could play the imitation game so well that an average interrogator would not have more than a 70 percent chance of a right identification after five minutes of questioning
